How I Think

Most brands hire a copywriter.
What they actually need is a strategist.

Here's what I see happen constantly.

A brand hires someone to write emails. The emails get written. Some of them are even good. But revenue barely moves.

Because the emails aren't the problem.

The ad sent cold traffic to the wrong page. The welcome sequence treated a buyer the same as a browser. The sales page had no message continuity from the ad that brought them there. The cart abandonment email fired three days after someone already purchased somewhere else.

Each piece existed in isolation. Doing its own thing. Talking to no one in particular.

That is what I fix.

I look at the whole system first. Where attention is being lost. Where trust is breaking down. Where the offer is failing to land. Then I build the version that actually connects, from the first scroll-stop to the sale to the post-purchase sequence that turns buyers into repeat customers.

Not just copy. A system that converts.

Before: Dead List. Emails in Spam. $0 Revenue.

Real Klaviyo data. Campaigns sent to 5,000+ people generating zero revenue.

After: 71% Open Rate. 61% CTR. $85K+ in Under 60 Days.

Same list. Fixed infrastructure. Revived segmentation. Website crashed from traffic volume.

1

The real problem nobody saw

8 to 14% open rates. Near zero clicks. Emails going straight to spam. Revenue from the list close to zero.

The obvious move was to rewrite the subject lines. That would have been completely wrong.

Before touching a single word, I ran a full deliverability audit. SPF and DKIM were misconfigured. DMARC wasn't set. Domain reputation had been damaged from years of sending to a disengaged list. No copy fix repairs broken infrastructure.

2

Fix the foundation before sending anything

  • Rebuilt SPF records with authorized sending partners only
  • Configured DKIM signing correctly through the ESP
  • Set DMARC policy with proper monitoring before enforcement
  • Removed spam trigger patterns from all campaign templates
3

Segmentation strategy before any promotional send

Split the list by real engagement: completely unengaged (90+ days), recently lapsed (30 to 60 days), occasionally active. Each segment received a different re-engagement sequence, not one blast to everyone.

Emails written to generate positive signals: opens, clicks, and replies. The strongest engagement signal you can send Gmail's algorithm.

4

Promotional calendar built and executed on a repaired foundation

Once reputation was climbing and engagement was restored, I built and executed a full promotional calendar. Sequenced sends to warm segments. Conversion-focused copy on infrastructure that actually delivered.

Result: 71% open rate. 61% click rate. 500% conversion increase. $85,000+ revenue in under 60 days. The client's website crashed from the traffic volume.

Ad Creative Project

Writing for one of the biggest voices in business.

Three ads. One offer. Three completely different psychological entry points. All in the same founder voice.

Facebook and Instagram Ads, Contrarian Thinking / Codie Sanchez

3 Ad Variations for Codie Sanchez's Main Street Millionaire Masterclass

Three conversion-focused ad variations for one of the most recognized business education brands in direct response. Each written in Codie's documented voice: direct, data-driven, zero fluff. Reviewed and approved internally by the brand team.

The strategic challenge: find three completely different psychological entry points into the same audience for the same offer, without losing the founder's voice in any of them.

Ad 1: Risk Reframe

Flipped the risk narrative using real acquisition data. 80% success rate for business acquisitions vs 10% for startups. Made the safe choice look like the dangerous one.

Ad 2: Economic Urgency

Built urgency around the K-shaped economy and the boomer retirement wave creating a once-in-a-generation window for acquisition buyers right now.

Ad 3: Decision Paralysis

Attacked analysis paralysis using Codie's Pick A Date philosophy. Framing inaction, not the purchase, as the actual risk the reader was taking.
